items.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes
items.excerpt: Vanderbilt's MutexaGPT uses LLM agents to turn plain-language, intuition-based enzyme requests into physics-based enzyme models and proposed mutations (Nature Computational Science).
items.rationale: Freshest item in the pool, peer-reviewed (Nature Computational Science): LLM agents turn plain-language intuition into physics-based enzyme design, a new research workflow.

items.title: New AI tool helps scientists identify bacteria hidden in soil
items.excerpt: BBERT, a DNA language model, classifies 100-base soil-DNA fragments as bacterial (~90% accuracy) and finds reading frames (~96%) without reference databases, cutting genome reconstruction from ~66 to 25 hours (Nucleic Acids Research).
items.rationale: Reference-free DNA language model with hard numbers (90%/96%, 66h to 25h) in Nucleic Acids Research; microbial ecology, no soil-metagenomics story in history.

items.title: AI often passes for human, but asking follow-up questions can trip it up
items.excerpt: In 72,000+ judgments of output from 636 people and 37 AI models across six language and vision tasks, judges often mistook AI for human, but live follow-up questioning exposed chatbots better as conversations grew longer (Nature Human Behaviour).
items.rationale: Large-scale Nature Human Behaviour study (72,000+ judgments, 37 models) with a usable finding: follow-up questioning unmasks AI. A distinct study from the 10-21 Turing-test dispute piece.

items.title: Space outposts beyond the Moon may rely on planetary AI
items.excerpt: Ohio State's LUMINA builds on lunar vision-language model LLaVA-LE to plan multistep analyses, rank candidate lunar landing sites and explain its evidence (presented at AAS DPS 58).
items.rationale: New planetary-science AI system (LUMINA, AAS DPS 58) that ranks lunar landing sites and explains its evidence; fills the astronomy slot and adds a third outlet.

items.title: AI framework cuts computing use by two-thirds while more than tripling success in virtual tasks
items.excerpt: SKKU's SAG lets an agent gauge its own uncertainty and request feedback only when worth it, cutting compute to about a third and raising virtual-task success from 24.6% to 78.3%; companion VAN-Flow RL filters lucky successes (NeurIPS 2026).
items.rationale: NeurIPS 2026 method with concrete gains (compute cut to about a third, success 24.6% to 78.3%) from uncertainty-aware feedback requests; new agent-learning result, no prior coverage.
